title: Risk Assessment: decompose 19 oversize Python files until the size allowlist is empty (#3312)
summary: Technical risk assessment for the full #3312 decomposition program as scoped by the operator (all 19 files in scope, no descope, empty `files:` allowlist as the binding acceptance criterion, `_run_pipeline` tackled head-on, pure refactor). Grounded against the live worktree at HEAD 3b1a97c30 and the confirmed refine analysis. This is a PURE-REFACTOR program, so the dominant risks are not algorithmic but mechanical-at-scale: (1) preserving the large test patch-target back-compat surface through barrel re-exports (57 distinct `routes.pipelines.*` targets across 137 test files; ~6-12 `gateway.gateway.*`); (2) extracting the `_run_pipeline` phase-transition state machine (pipelines.py:23345) without behavior drift; and a NEWLY-SURFACED, high-impact mechanical risk the refine analysis did not cover — (3) several in-scope files are copied into their container images by a top-level `*.py` glob or as a single explicit file, so converting them to sub-packages SILENTLY breaks the image while `make lint` + `make test-all` stay GREEN, because the size lint and unit tests run against the source tree, not the built image. Overall risk MEDIUM. The work is well-precedented (pattern doc + select_tests reference + merged PR #2335) and every individual slice is small, but the program is long, serially ratcheted, and edits shared conflict-hotspot files (the allowlist + CLAUDE.md seam tables) from many in-flight slices. Recommendation: PROCEED_WITH_MITIGATIONS.
scope_note: Grounded against the confirmed refine analysis (.egg-state/drafts/3312-analysis.md + 3312-analysis-human.md), the live issue task_description (all 19 files, empty allowlist, no descope), the working tree on 2026-06-26 (HEAD 3b1a97c30), the canonical pattern (docs/guides/decomposition-pattern.md), the worked reference (scripts/select_tests/), and both container Dockerfiles. The architect/task_planner plan artifacts (3312-plan*.md/json, 3312-architect-slices.yaml) were NOT yet present on this branch when this assessment was drafted (all producers still WORKING in parallel). Risks are framed against the issue's work program and the real touchpoints; reconcile each against the planner's slice DAG on review — see plan_reconciliation_pending. Reviewer (risk_analyst also reviews in plan) must check the planner's slices against R1-R3 mitigations specifically before ACK.

risks.title: Test patch-target back-compat surface — a dropped barrel re-export breaks tests
risks.description: Non-negotiables #2/#3: the barrel is the stable API and existing `patch("routes.pipelines._foo")` targets must keep resolving. 57 distinct symbols are patched through `routes.pipelines` across 137 test files; ~6-12 through `gateway.gateway`. Per the pattern doc (line 87): 'A submodule extraction that drops the barrel re-export is a bug.' A single missed re-export surfaces as `AttributeError: module 'routes.pipelines' has no attribute '_foo'` in whatever test patches `_foo` — and ONLY in that test, so it is easy to miss in a partial run. The dominant surface is pipelines.py; gateway.py is smaller but same shape.
risks.mitigation: Per cluster, run the section-(d) external-importer + patch-target grep audit BEFORE extracting, and re-export EVERY symbol with any external reference (public or underscore-private) through the sub-package __init__.py. Reviewer must confirm each slice's __init__.py re-export list covers the audited targets. `make test-all` (not narrowed `make test`) green at every landing is the backstop — the planner must mandate test-all at each boundary, since a narrowed run can skip the one test that patches the dropped symbol.

risks.title: _run_pipeline phase-transition state machine — behavior drift in a pure-refactor program
risks.description: pipelines.py:23345 `_run_pipeline` is a stateful loop driving phase transitions inside a 27k-line file. Non-negotiable #7 forbids deferring it; non-negotiable (pure refactor) forbids behavior change. Mechanical line-extraction will not work — the loop carries control flow, shared local state, and ordering that a naive per-phase split can subtly reorder. This is simultaneously the hardest extraction AND the highest behavior-change blast radius (it sequences every pipeline's lifecycle). A latent reorder here is exactly the kind of regression a 'we only moved things' review is least likely to catch.
risks.mitigation: Treat _run_pipeline as its own isolated multi-step cluster (per-phase handlers behind preserved signatures + a thin orchestration loop, the pattern doc's prior design). Require characterization/behavioral tests around the loop landed BEFORE the extraction so a drift is caught. Land it late (after the independent files de-risk the recipe) but DO NOT drop it. Reviewer scrutinizes this slice's diff for any non-mechanical change (reordered calls, changed early-returns, merged branches). If a real bug is found, file a separate `Part of #3312` issue — never bundle (see R7).

risks.title: Dockerfile COPY breaks for sub-package conversions while lint + test-all stay GREEN
risks.description: NEWLY SURFACED (refine analysis did not cover this). Several in-scope files are NOT copied by a recursive directory COPY: (a) the 5 top-level orchestrator modules — gateway_client.py, kubernetes_spawner.py, mcp_tools.py, peer_consensus.py, state_store.py — ship via `COPY orchestrator/*.py ./`, a glob that does NOT recurse into a new sub-package directory; (b) the 3 gateway files — gateway.py, worktree_manager.py, git_client.py — ship via `COPY gateway/*.py ./`, same non-recursive glob; (c) sandbox/entrypoint.py ships as a SINGLE explicit file to a bin path (`COPY sandbox/entrypoint.py /usr/local/bin/entrypoint.py`) and is invoked as that file. When any of these becomes a `foo/` sub-package, the package directory is NOT copied into the image -> ModuleNotFoundError at container runtime. The insidious part: the binding 'green at every landing' gate (`make lint` + `make test-all`) runs against the SOURCE TREE, not the built image, so it can stay fully GREEN while the shipped image is broken. The routes/ files (pipelines, signals, deployment, phases, decisions, event_prompt) are SAFE — `COPY orchestrator/routes/ ./routes/` is recursive. entrypoint.py is additionally awkward: it is invoked as an executable file, so it likely must stay a thin shim re-exporting from a sub-package located elsewhere rather than itself becoming a package.
risks.mitigation: Planner MUST add a Dockerfile-COPY task to every slice that converts a top-level-glob or single-file-COPY target into a sub-package: add `COPY orchestrator/<pkg>/ ./<pkg>/` (or gateway equivalent) in the SAME slice as the extraction. For sandbox/entrypoint.py, keep entrypoint.py as a thin executable shim importing the new sub-package, or update both the COPY and the invocation path together. CONFIRM the sandbox egg_lib packaging mechanism (no COPY found for egg_lib/ — verify orch_cli.py/contract_cli.py reach the image via pip/setuptools find_packages before assuming sub-packages are auto-included). Add an image-build or integration smoke check to the landing gate for these specific slices so a missing COPY is caught, since test-all alone will not catch it.

risks.title: A sub-module itself over the cap re-trips the lint after the allowlist entry is dropped
risks.description: Acceptance is an EMPTY allowlist. The lint ratchet forbids adding a fresh allowlist entry for 'this new submodule is also over the cap' (pattern section g; a new entry directly contradicts the issue's empty-allowlist goal). select_tests/_graph.py at 52KB is a live example of a sub-module that lands large. For the giants (pipelines.py 27k, gateway.py 10k), a single decomposition pass plausibly produces sub-modules still over 1,500 lines / 100KB, which re-trips the lint the moment the parent's allowlist entry is removed.
risks.mitigation: Planner sizes every target sub-module under the cap during cluster design and PRE-ALLOCATES the expected further-splits per cluster (pattern section g). The rule is hard: further-split in-slice, NEVER add a new allowlist entry. If a non-obvious further-split is needed, escalate via HITL (pattern section g) rather than allowlisting. Reviewer checks that no slice adds an allowlist key.

risks.title: Shared conflict-hotspot files — allowlist + CLAUDE.md seam tables edited by many in-flight slices
risks.description: Every slice edits scripts/file-size-allowlist.yaml (delete its one key) and a CLAUDE.md seam table (orchestrator/, gateway/, sandbox/, or the new shared/CLAUDE.md). With ~19+ slices and parallel landings, these shared files are guaranteed rebase-conflict points. The pattern doc (section e) explicitly calls the allowlist conflict 'expected' on rebase. Mishandled conflicts can silently re-add a removed entry or drop a seam row.
risks.mitigation: Each slice touches ONLY its own allowlist key and its own seam row — single-key delete, single-row add, no reflow of unrelated lines (minimizes conflict surface). Follow the pattern doc's section-(e) rebase recipe (re-resolve the allowlist conflict by re-deleting your key, re-run the lint to confirm the allowlist still matches reality). Sequence landings rather than racing many through the same file simultaneously where the DAG allows. Reviewer diff-checks that exactly one allowlist key was removed and no unrelated entry changed.

risks.title: 'Green at every landing' couples to image breakage and serialized test-all cost/flakiness
risks.description: The binding gate is `make lint` + `make test-all` green at EVERY landing boundary (acceptance #3). Two issues: (a) test-all green does NOT prove the image is intact (see R3) — the gate has a blind spot for COPY breakage; (b) over 19+ serialized landings, full test-all on each boundary is expensive and any pre-existing flaky test can falsely block or be falsely waved through, eroding the 'green at every boundary' guarantee.
risks.mitigation: For the R3-affected slices, add an image-build/integration smoke step to the per-landing gate. Treat any test-all failure at a boundary as blocking (do not land on red); if a failure is a known pre-existing flake, quarantine it as a separate `Part of #3312` follow-up rather than waving the landing through. Keep slices small so each boundary's test-all delta is reviewable.

risks.title: Pure-refactor discipline — bug fixes bundled into 'we only moved things' PRs
risks.description: Non-negotiable: pure refactor, no behavior change; bugs surfaced get a SEPARATE follow-up (`Part of #3312`), never bundled. A 27k-line file (and a 10k gateway) almost certainly hide latent bugs a coder will notice mid-extraction. The temptation to 'fix while moving' introduces behavior change into a diff reviewed as mechanical, making the review unsound and the regression risk invisible.
risks.mitigation: Every slice's task text states the pure-refactor rule explicitly. Reviewer scans each diff for non-mechanical changes (logic edits, reordered/added/removed calls, changed conditionals) and NACKs any behavior change found in a decomposition slice, directing it to a separate follow-up. Characterization tests (R2) catch unintended behavior deltas.

risks.title: Seam-table acceptance criterion mis-scoped — no live #2261 rows to 'retag'
risks.description: The issue (status + non-negotiable #6) asserts orchestrator/CLAUDE.md and gateway/CLAUDE.md still carry stale `#2261` slice tags / placeholder TBD rows to retag. The refiner verified this is NOT true of the live tree — those files have only a component-overview table + a generic decompose paragraph; the live #2261 refs are in docs/, not the seam tables. A planner task literally worded 'retag the #2261 rows' would have no target and could be marked blocked/failed.
risks.mitigation: Planner frames acceptance #5 as 'ADD concrete submodule seam rows per landing + ADD a sandbox/CLAUDE.md seam table + CREATE shared/CLAUDE.md covering plan_parser.py' — NOT 'retag #2261 rows.' Honor the literal #2261 wording only opportunistically against the docs/ files (optional, non-gating). Binding criterion: concrete seam coverage exists for every in-scope file at its landing.

risks.title: Program-completion risk — the two giants stall while the empty-allowlist criterion stays unmet
risks.description: Acceptance is a fully EMPTY allowlist. If pipelines.py (27k, with _run_pipeline) or gateway.py (10k) stalls, the program cannot satisfy its binding criterion even though the other 17 files landed. This is a completion/throughput risk, not a correctness one. Scope is LOCKED — the giants must NOT be descoped to escape it (explicit operator directive).
risks.mitigation: Planner applies the issue's own ordering heuristic: front-load the 17 independent per-file slices so they land value early and de-risk the recipe, while keeping the giants in scope as their own multi-slice clusters with internal checkpoints so partial progress is visible. Do NOT drop the giants. If a giant genuinely cannot land after honest effort, that is a HITL escalation about the program, never a silent descope.

risks.title: New seam artifacts forgotten — shared/CLAUDE.md creation + sandbox/ seam table + test-layout drift
risks.description: Acceptance #5 requires CREATING shared/CLAUDE.md (currently ABSENT) for plan_parser.py and ADDING a seam table to sandbox/CLAUDE.md (exists, no seam table today). Non-negotiable #10 (guidance, not a hard 1:1 gate): tests keep using the barrel surface so they don't move when internal layout shifts. Low engineering risk; the failure mode is simply forgetting a new-file/new-section deliverable or needlessly relocating tests.
risks.mitigation: Planner attaches the seam-artifact deliverable to the specific slice that lands each relevant file (plan_parser -> create shared/CLAUDE.md; first sandbox file -> add sandbox/ seam table). Tests stay on the barrel surface; only add matching tests/.../foo/ sub-packages where the mapping is clean (non-negotiable #10 is guidance). Reviewer confirms the seam artifact exists at the landing that introduces the corresponding sub-package.

reviewer_checklist_for_plan: R1: every cluster has a section-(d) patch-target audit task; __init__.py re-export lists cover the audited targets; make test-all (not narrowed) mandated at each boundary.
R2: _run_pipeline is its own cluster with preserved-signature per-phase handlers + characterization tests landed before extraction; not deferred, not descoped.

R3: every slice converting a top-level-glob orchestrator/gateway module or sandbox single-file-COPY target into a sub-package includes the matching Dockerfile COPY update IN THE SAME SLICE; entrypoint.py stays a thin executable shim or COPY+invocation updated together; egg_lib packaging mechanism confirmed; image/integration smoke added to those landing gates.
R4: no slice adds a new allowlist key; over-cap sub-modules are further-split in-slice; sized under cap during planning.
R5: each slice removes exactly one allowlist key + adds one seam row, minimal-diff; section-(e) rebase recipe referenced.
R7: every slice text carries the pure-refactor / no-behavior-change / separate-follow-up rule.
R8: seam criterion worded as ADD/CREATE, not 'retag #2261'.
R9: ordering front-loads the 17 independents; giants retained as checkpointed clusters; no descope.
R10: shared/CLAUDE.md creation + sandbox/ seam table attached to the right landing slices.
